label: Original-phase input of g/r/t/y/s/u/i/x/j/e/n after an earlier l/z/k/b/q/w
predicate: (phase == 0) & (t >= 2) & isin(in_tok, [tok(c) for c in "grtysuixjen"]) & seen([tok(c) for c in "lzkbqw"])
explanation: About 95% of activation mass falls in the original (input) phase at t>=2, and the rate rises with position. It never fires at t=0 and almost never on <DEL> or during the copy phase (5% of mass, mostly at recall_idx 1). It is driven by the current input token, strongest for g (4.5x lift), then r, t, y, s, and weaker for u, i, x, j, e, n and 0. It is boosted when tokens from a second set (l, z, k, b, q, w, and to a lesser degree 2 and 3) appeared earlier in the sequence, especially as the first token: the top activations are almost all g/r/t/y inputs in sequences starting with l or z. It prefers the first occurrence of the input token. The two factors behave like a graded additive tuning, not a clean rule, so precision is limited (dev F1 about 0.55, mass recall 0.79). Many weak activations come from other tokens, and many predicted steps stay below threshold.
